name: Cross-platform mobile: Expo + React Native
use_cases: A single product team ships an iOS and Android client against a separately owned API
The team can share most screens and application logic while retaining platform-specific behavior where needed
The product needs native device features available through Expo SDK or compatible React Native modules
choose_when: Both iOS and Android are required and sharing a TypeScript/React codebase is more useful than two platform-native UI codebases
The team accepts per-platform native builds, permissions, credentials, testing and store releases
Required native libraries support the selected Expo SDK and can be tested in a development build
avoid_when: The product requires deeply platform-specific interfaces or capabilities that make most UI and behavior separate; choose SwiftUI and/or Kotlin with Compose
The team cannot build or obtain representative iOS and Android development builds and test both platforms
The project assumes Expo Go includes arbitrary native libraries or considers one shared codebase proof of equivalent platform behavior

tools.default: React Native with the Expo SDK and the generated Expo Router baseline
tools.alternatives: Platform-specific route files or native modules for behavior that must differ by operating system; Flutter is a conditional alternative when a team accepts Dart and needs a custom rendered interface across more platforms, not a default substitute
tools.reason: One TypeScript project can share much of the UI and application logic across iOS and Android while using native UI components and platform APIs
tools.limits: Shared source does not guarantee identical layout, accessibility, lifecycle or device behavior. Expo Router and the default template evolve with the selected SDK; preserve and verify the generated compatible versions.

tools.default: A separately selected backend/API with versioned request and response contracts; use Fetch behind an injected client and validate untrusted responses at runtime
tools.alternatives: Generate a TypeScript client from an owned OpenAPI schema only when generation and versioning are established in the actual project
tools.reason: The native clients should share service contracts without moving data ownership, authorization or durable work into the installed app
tools.limits: TypeScript types do not validate network data at runtime. The client is public and cannot keep provider credentials or backend secrets. Choose the backend separately from this mobile profile.

tools.default: Keep server-owned data behind the API; add local persistence only for a stated cache or offline requirement
tools.alternatives: Expo SQLite for structured local data when query, retention and migration requirements justify it; a query cache only when remote loading and invalidation need it
tools.reason: Separating remote authority from device storage makes offline behavior, retries and reconciliation explicit
tools.limits: Local storage does not create synchronization, conflict resolution, cross-device truth or encryption by itself. Define offline reads and writes separately.

tools.default: expo-secure-store for small locally held session credentials when its platform behavior and backup policy fit
tools.alternatives: In-memory credentials when persistence is unnecessary; use platform security APIs through a reviewed library for a different storage requirement
tools.reason: Sensitive user credentials need an operating-system-backed storage boundary rather than app preferences or source code
tools.limits: SecureStore is not a backend secret vault or a general database. Define logout, expiry, revocation, device migration and backup behavior; server authorization remains authoritative.

tools.default: Use the Expo SDK or a React Native library that explicitly supports both target platforms and the selected SDK
tools.alternatives: A config plugin or local Expo module when an app-specific native extension is necessary
tools.reason: Expo config and development builds can include native capabilities while retaining the JavaScript development workflow
tools.limits: Expo Go contains a fixed set of native libraries. A module with native code that is absent from Expo Go needs a development build; native support, permissions and version compatibility must be checked per platform.

tools.default: Use the Expo CLI included with the project, `npx expo install` for compatible native package versions, the committed lockfile and `npx expo-doctor`
tools.alternatives: Keep generated native directories and use native IDE workflows only when the project adopts direct native changes or needs native debugging
tools.reason: React Native packages must match the Expo SDK's native dependency set; the doctor command checks common project and version issues
tools.limits: A clean doctor report is not a successful iOS or Android build, device test or release. Re-run native builds when native dependencies, app configuration or plugins change.

tools.default: Development builds for real application work; build and verify iOS and Android separately. Use local Xcode/Android tooling or an explicitly chosen cloud build service.
tools.alternatives: Expo Go for initial experiments with only the native libraries it already includes; EAS Build is optional, not required by Expo itself
tools.reason: Development builds include the project's actual native dependencies; EAS can perform cloud builds without a local native toolchain
tools.limits: Local iOS builds require macOS and Xcode; local Android builds require Android Studio/SDK and a compatible Java toolchain. Cloud builds do not remove Apple/Google account, application identity, signing, credential custody, store policy, per-platform device testing or release ownership.

tools.default: Unit-test domain/API behavior; exercise navigation, permissions, lifecycle, offline/reconnect and accessibility in development builds on both platforms
tools.alternatives: Use simulators/emulators for broad repeatable checks and representative physical devices for hardware, permission and release behavior
tools.reason: The shared JavaScript code still runs inside two operating-system-specific native applications
tools.limits: A simulator/emulator or Expo Go check does not qualify device hardware, signing, native-module behavior or store distribution. Test against the minimum supported OS and current supported OS versions.

setup_steps: Start in a local source workspace and read its README, package manager, lockfile, runtime pins and instructions. Confirm this is a new, unused destination; never run a new-project generator over an existing app.

Record supported iOS/Android versions and devices, app identifiers, API contract, required permissions/native capabilities, offline behavior and who owns signing and releases. Select the backend separately; this client does not supply one.

Install a supported Node.js LTS and inspect `npx create-expo-app@latest --help`. The 23 October 2026 CLI 5.1.5 help exposes `--no-agents-md` but no `--no-git` option. Use an absent destination and check whether the generated project owns a nested Git repository before adopting it into a monorepo.

Create the project with the explicit `default@sdk-58` template after reviewing its options. Expo documents that during the SDK 58 transition, `@latest` without `--template` creates SDK 57; pin the template when SDK 58 is intended. Pass `--no-agents-md` to avoid generating AGENTS.md or Claude settings. Inspect README, package.json, app config, routes, lockfile and generated Git state before editing; record the resolved Expo/React Native/React versions and template.

Install and lock dependencies. Use `npx expo install` for Expo/React Native native packages, verify the SDK compatibility matrix and run `npx expo-doctor`. Do not add a native dependency until its iOS and Android support, config plugin and SDK compatibility are checked.

Start with the Expo Router/app-config baseline and a development build for each target. Expo Go is a limited playground; a custom native module, app identity/configuration change or native dependency requires a project-specific build.

Implement a versioned API client and explicit loading/error/auth states. Put domain data, authorization, provider credentials and durable jobs in the selected backend. Add local data only with a stated offline/cache policy and migration plan.

Test both iOS and Android: navigation/back behavior, foreground/background and process restart, permission granted/denied/revoked, session expiry/logout, network interruption, offline reads/writes, large text and screen readers. Keep tests for shared logic, but do not let them stand in for native verification.

Prepare development, preview and production builds with explicit app identifiers, signing owner, version/build-number policy and credential custody. Verify install/update and API compatibility on both platforms; publication is a separate authorized release step.
evidence_status: Documentation reviewed 23 October 2026. The explicit `default@sdk-58` template was generated with create-expo-app 5.1.5; npm install succeeded, Expo Doctor passed 20/20, and `expo export --platform ios` produced a JavaScript bundle. Generated lint and TypeScript checks failed; no native build, device/simulator behavior, application integration, signing or store release was qualified.

sources.title: Expo: Create a project
sources.claim: Expo documents the official Expo and React Native project initializer and the default template workflow.

sources.title: Expo Router introduction
sources.claim: Expo Router provides file-based routing for Expo applications across supported platforms.

sources.title: Expo SDK version reference
sources.claim: The Expo SDK reference documents package APIs by SDK version; native package choices must match the project SDK.

sources.title: Expo SQLite
sources.claim: Expo SQLite provides local relational storage; it does not define synchronization, conflict resolution or server authority.

sources.title: Expo data fetching
sources.claim: Expo documents client data-fetching patterns; the application still needs an explicit API and server authority.

sources.title: Expo SecureStore
sources.claim: Expo SecureStore exposes platform-specific secure key-value storage with documented limits; it is not a substitute for server-side authorization.

sources.title: React Native security
sources.claim: React Native security guidance treats the app as a client that cannot safely hold secrets or enforce server authorization.

sources.title: Expo: Add custom native code
sources.claim: Expo documents generated native project customization and config plugins for repeatable native configuration.

sources.title: Expo development builds
sources.claim: Expo development builds contain a project-specific native dependency set, unlike the fixed Expo Go client.

sources.title: Expo CLI
sources.claim: Expo CLI provides project development commands; inspect the selected SDK and current CLI behavior before relying on a command.

sources.title: Expo tools and Expo Doctor
sources.claim: Expo Doctor checks project configuration and dependency compatibility; its result does not replace native builds or device tests.

sources.title: Expo build troubleshooting and SDK compatibility checks
sources.claim: Expo troubleshooting guidance covers SDK compatibility and native build diagnostics.

sources.title: Develop an app with Expo
sources.claim: Expo separates JavaScript iteration, native project generation and local or cloud native builds.

sources.title: EAS Build introduction
sources.claim: EAS Build is an optional hosted native build service; using it does not establish device or release qualification.

sources.title: EAS Submit introduction
sources.claim: EAS Submit is a separate app-store delivery workflow requiring platform release configuration and ownership.

sources.title: Expo unit testing
sources.claim: Expo documents unit testing setup for application logic; unit tests do not qualify native platform behavior.

sources.title: React Native platform-specific code
sources.claim: React Native supports platform-specific APIs and file variants when iOS and Android behavior differs.

sources.title: React Native accessibility
sources.claim: React Native provides accessibility APIs, but each platform and supported device still needs product-specific accessibility testing.

sources.title: Flutter multi-platform support (conditional alternative)
sources.claim: Flutter documents supported platform integrations; adopting Flutter adds Dart and a distinct rendering/toolchain choice.

sources.title: Expo: create-expo-app, template pinning and SDK 58 transition
sources.claim: During the SDK 58 transition, Expo documents that unqualified create-expo-app@latest creates SDK 57 and recommends --template default@sdk-58 when SDK 58 is intended.

open_questions: Which iOS and Android versions, phone/tablet form factors and devices are actually supported?
Does the product need offline reads, offline writes or conflict resolution, and what is the authoritative data owner?
Which API, identity provider, native SDKs, app links, notifications and permission flows are required?
Which custom native libraries/config plugins are required, and are exact versions supported by the selected Expo SDK on both platforms?
Who owns Apple and Google application identities, developer accounts, signing credentials, build service access and store release?
